title: Run of the Syntax Scan
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $n$ be a natural number, let $q$ be a syntax-automaton state, and let $st$ be a seven-register state. If $st.P+n=|x|$, every register of $st$ is at most $B$, and $|x|\le B$, then there is a finite run from the syntax-scanning label with automaton state $q$ and registers $st$ to the input-exhausted label with automaton state obtained by folding the suffix of $x$ beginning at position $st.P$ through the syntax transition, and with the input pointer set to $|x|$ and every other register unchanged. Every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the program guard and register bound $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $st$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B,n$ natural numbers, $q$ a syntax-automaton state, and $st$ a
seven-register state. If $st.P+n=|x|$, every register of $st$ is at most $B$, and
$|x|\le B$, then the program has a finite run from the syntax-scanning label with state
$q$ and register values $st$ to the input-exhausted label with automaton state obtained
by scanning the suffix of $x$ starting at position $st.P$ from $q$, and with all
registers unchanged except that $P=|x|$. Every configuration before the endpoint
satisfies the program’s precondition and register bound $B$.
